## architecture_facade_concept

> Conceptual exterior facade rendering for an architecture studio's project poster.

**Artifact:** `poster`, `1536x1024`, aspect `3:2`
**Demo vars:** `templates/architecture/_vars_examples/architecture_facade_concept.yml`

### English

```
[1. Subject] A wide 3:2 conceptual exterior facade rendering of a building project titled "Tide Pavilion", sited in Northern coastal town and authored by Atlas + Verde Studio. The frame presents the primary public elevation as a confident architectural portrait — the building reads as the single hero subject, with site and sky kept restrained.
[2. Action] The composition asserts the design intent at first glance: massing, material rhythm, and fenestration pattern carry the read. There is no pedestrian narrative, no interior glimpse, no construction process — the building itself stands as a finished statement, photographed as if on a calm overcast morning.
[3. Scene] Generic civic surroundings appropriate to Northern coastal town: a low foreground plinth of paving, a quiet adjacent street edge, distant blurred massing suggesting urban context. Soft diffused daylight (post-2010 coastal modernism sensibility), no bright sun, no theatrical sky, no flag of any nation, no recognisable landmark.
[4. Composition] Horizontal 3:2 frame. The facade occupies the central 70% of the image width, top of the building landing near the upper third line. Ground plane runs along the lower 18%. A small project title plate sits in the lower-left margin and a studio credit line rests at the lower right; both are part of the composition rather than overlay chrome.
[5. Style] Architectural-rendering aesthetic — closer to a competition board visualization than a magazine photograph. Material palette anchored on weathered timber, board-formed concrete, slate, with restrained ambient shadows, crisp edge lines, and subtle physical-camera lens character. No painterly treatment, no neon, no film-grain stylisation.

Text to render exactly (chunked into named slots):
- project_name: "Tide Pavilion"
- location: "Northern coastal town"
- studio_credit: "Atlas + Verde Studio"

NO: real famous buildings, real-architect likeness, identifiable city skylines, recognisable national flags, human models in fashion poses, lens flare, rainbow gradient skies, HDR oversaturation, watermarks, signatures
```

## architecture_presentation_board

> Multi-panel architecture presentation board combining concept, diagram, render, and short text.

**Artifact:** `infographic`, `1920x1088`, aspect `16:9`
**Demo vars:** `templates/architecture/_vars_examples/architecture_presentation_board.yml`

### English

```
[1. Subject] A 16:9 architecture presentation board for the project "Hillside Reading Pavilion" (2026). The board is a single composite artifact partitioned into four labelled panels: a concept sketch, a small site diagram, a hero exterior render, and a short typographic statement. It reads as one page from a competition portfolio.
[2. Action] The viewer's eye must move predictably from the concept panel to the diagram, into the hero render, and finally rest on the typographic block carrying the keywords stacked reading rooms above a public porch and cross-laminated timber on a stone plinth. No motion, no narrative people — the board itself is the deliverable.
[3. Scene] Document-grade portfolio surface. Warm bone paper field with fine paper grain; each panel sits inside its own quiet frame with generous breathing room. No physical setting, no perspective beyond what lives inside the render panel itself.
[4. Composition] 16:9 frame partitioned into a 2x2 grid of unequal panels. Upper-left (~28% width) holds the concept sketch panel. Upper-right (~72% width) holds the hero render. Lower-left holds the small site diagram. Lower-right holds the typography block (title, year, two keywords). A 4% gutter and a 6% outer margin separate the panels cleanly.
[5. Style] Studio-portfolio editorial aesthetic. Palette: bone-paper ground, slate ink, one warm accent (terracotta or ochre, drawn from CLT, weathered limestone, brushed brass). Type system: a humanist serif for the project title, a geometric sans-serif for captions. Hairline 1px rules around panels, no drop shadows, no decorative gradients, no 3D extrusion.

Text to render exactly (chunked into named slots):
- project_title: "Hillside Reading Pavilion (2026)"
- concept_keyword: "Concept: stacked reading rooms above a public porch"
- structure_keyword: "Structure: cross-laminated timber on a stone plinth"

NO: real famous buildings, real-architect likeness, identifiable city skylines, photo-real cityscape backgrounds, lens flare, rainbow gradients, HDR oversaturation, watermarks, signatures, 3D extruded text
```

## architecture_site_diagram

> Site plan / urban-context diagram with three labeled zones, drawn in plan view.

**Artifact:** `diagram`, `1920x1088`, aspect `16:9`
**Demo vars:** `templates/architecture/_vars_examples/architecture_site_diagram.yml`

### English

```
[1. Subject] A wide 16:9 architectural site-plan diagram for "Riverbend Civic Block", drawn in orthographic plan view from directly above. The diagram reads as a technical document — building footprints, hatched ground textures, a north arrow, and a graphic scale bar (calibrated to 1:500) anchor it as a real planning artifact.
[2. Action] The diagram must communicate a parti at a glance: the eye lands on public plaza & market first, then traces movement axes through civic library wing and arrives at riverwalk landscape edge. There is no perspective view, no sky, no photographic texture — only the flat top-down logic of a working site plan.
[3. Scene] Document-grade plan surface — flat warm-paper field with a faint drafting-grid underprint. No people, no cars, no theatrical lighting. Trees are abstracted as soft circles, water as a calm hatched field, paving as fine dotted grain.
[4. Composition] 16:9 frame. Top ~8% is a title band carrying the site name and a small north arrow at the top-right. The plan occupies the central ~78% of the canvas, padded with generous margins. The three zones are labelled in-place with thin leader lines, set in small caps. Bottom ~10% holds a graphic scale bar and a quiet legend strip.
[5. Style] Urban-design plan-graphic aesthetic — closer to a planning-jury board than a marketing render. Restrained palette: warm bone paper ground, cool slate building footprints, a single muted accent (oxidised teal) reserved for circulation arrows and the north symbol. Geometric sans- serif type, 1px hairline rules, no drop shadows, no 3D extrusion.

Text to render exactly (chunked into named slots):
- site_label: "Riverbend Civic Block"
- zone1: "Zone A — public plaza & market"
- zone2: "Zone B — civic library wing"
- zone3: "Zone C — riverwalk landscape edge"

NO: photographic textures, perspective views, real-city street grids, recognisable real landmarks, 3D extruded buildings, drop shadows, lens flare, rainbow palettes, watermarks, clip-art trees
```
